rules: Never edit the project while the IDE is online with the PLC (cts status: plc=online); run cts disconnect first.
A new object must be referenced by a task before downloading.
Never save over a client project; work on an owned copy.
Start the in-IDE agent in CODESYS: Tools > Scripting > Scripts > C > cds-text-sync, or from the CLI with 'cts project open --launch' (fresh IDE).

A modal IDE dialog blocks every command until it is answered. Read it with 'cts dialog' and answer it with 'cts dialog answer --choose ... --press ...' instead of waiting for a person -- see 'cts guide dialog'.
jobs: Change code: edit the .st files under project-view -> cts compare -> cts import --dry-run -> cts import -> cts build. The IDE then holds the change unsaved: cts save when the engineer wants it saved, cts commit -m MSG to record it in git.
Rename a variable, input or POU everywhere: grep -rn NAME project-view finds every use (the files are the project's text) -> edit them -> cts import -> cts build --all-objects.
Find why the build fails: cts build --all-objects names each error and its object (a plain cts build skips objects no task calls).
Keep an edit made in the IDE: cts compare names it (ide_changed) -> cts sync writes it into its file -> cts commit -m MSG.
Test logic without a PLC: the POU's .st at the top of project-view, its checks in PRG_Tests.st -> cts import -> cts test (cts guide tests sets the test application up).
Run ST unit tests: cts test (cts guide tests explains the simulation test application).
Put it on the PLC: cts build -> cts download; skip cts import when cts compare is clean (cts guide deploy).
Record how the plant runs, then analyse it: cts trend set VAR ... -> cts import -> cts build -> cts download -> cts trend on; later cts trend pull -> cts trend query SQL (cts guide trend).
Catch what happens now, before and after a fault: cts connect -> cts trace set VAR ... --trigger VAR -> cts trace start -> cts trace pull --wait N (cts guide trace).
